title: CIA Director Ratcliffe to Take Bigger Role in Russia-Ukraine Talks as Trump-Putin Call No Breakthrough
detail: Following a 'frank' Trump-Putin phone call, US officials said CIA Director John Ratcliffe is preparing to take a larger role in shuttle diplomacy between Moscow and Kyiv, with the White House considering paring back the involvement of special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who have led the talks. Ratcliffe is expected to maintain contact with intelligence officers in both countries while the envoys said they remained optimistic trilateral US-Russia-Ukraine talks (suspended since February) could resume, though people familiar with the discussions said Putin showed little sign of backing down from his existing demands. Overnight, Russia attacked Ukraine with 149 strike drones (Shahed, Gerbera, Parodiya decoys); Ukraine's Air Force said 128 were shot down or suppressed, with hits recorded at 13 locations including a UAV depot in Mykolaiv Oblast and port infrastructure in Chornomorsk and Odesa.

media.caption: Trump and Putin have held renewed phone talks as CIA Director Ratcliffe takes on a bigger negotiating role

title: Russian Strike on Pavlohrad Shopping Centre Kills 5, Injures 67
detail: Russia struck a busy shopping centre in central Pavlohrad, Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, around midday on September 10, when the streets were crowded. Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi said the attack killed 5 people, including 39-year-old miner Vitaliy Guba and 43-year-old DTEK machinist Yevhen Shevchenko, and injured at least 67, among them three teenage boys aged 13, 14 and 15. Cars, retail units and a shop caught fire in the blast.

title: Canada Pledges Over $2B in Air Defence, Energy and Drone Support During Zelenskyy Visit
detail: During President Zelenskyy's visit to Canada, Prime Minister Mark Carney announced CAN$350 million (about US$260 million) for Patriot missiles and F-16 ammunition through the US JUMPSTART programme, plus CAN$450 million in loan guarantees to repair Ukraine's energy infrastructure ahead of winter. Canada also agreed to direct 30% of its new drone production to Ukraine. Zelenskyy said the visit produced more than $2 billion in new Canadian support, including over $1 billion for defense, as the two countries signed a broader 'hundred-year partnership' agreement.

media.caption: Zelenskyy and Canadian PM Mark Carney announce a new Ukraine support package, Sept. 10, 2026
